evidence: EXEC SQL ... END-EXEC with embedded SQL (DB2/ODBC style)
88-level condition names with SET ... TO TRUE
COPY setupenv_openjensen and COPY z0100-error-routine (no REPLACING, GnuCOBOL convention)

purpose.summary: A CGI program that queries a student database to retrieve a list of courses and grades for a given student (user_id) and program (program_id). It fetches completed grades via a JOIN on tbl_course and tbl_grade, then fetches all courses in the program, writing results (course name, dates, grade, comment) as comma-separated records to a text file (betyg-elev.txt) for consumption by a PHP front-end.

notable_features: EXEC SQL with cursor-based fetching (DECLARE, OPEN, FETCH, CLOSE)
CGI-style program calling dynamic library routines (wui-print-header, wui-start-html, write-post-string, get-post-value, wui-end-html)
Output written to a LINE SEQUENTIAL flat file for PHP consumption
COPY directives for environment setup and error routine
Duplicate 01-level name 'wr-rec-vars' in DECLARE SECTION (potential compile issue)
In-memory array (OCCURS 25) used to track which courses have grades
Swedish-language identifiers and comments (betyg=grade, elev=student, kurs=course)
verdict.notes: The program has a likely bug: two separate 01-level items named 'wr-rec-vars' appear within the same EXEC SQL DECLARE SECTION, which would cause a duplicate name error in most compilers. The comment 'never never use a dash in cursor names' is notable and suggests awareness of GnuCOBOL/MySQL ESQL quirks. The domain is Swedish educational software (betyg=grade, elev=student). The COPY of 'setupenv_openjensen' suggests a development/test environment setup copybook. The second FETCH in B0210 is missing the :tbl_grade-course_id host variable, which is another likely bug.
